headline: US Sanctions Russian and North Korean IT Worker Money Laundering Scheme
technical: The US Treasury sanctioned Russian nationals Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov and Vitold Viktorovich Obertas, alongside North Korean entities like Amnokgang and Alis, for laundering millions in cryptocurrency. These funds were generated by North Korean IT workers using stolen identities to secure remote roles at US firms, utilizing AI tools for hiring and funnencing illicit operations.

headline: Researcher finds zero-click code execution flaw in Telegram stickers on iOS
technical: Researcher Saifeldeen Aziz discovered zero-click memory corruption and logic bugs in Telegram's sticker handling, involving the rlottie library (CVE-2026-111105). A numeric truncation flaw in rlottie allows writes before memory buffers, enabling remote code execution across iOS, Android, and Desktop clients without user interaction. Telegram previously disputed related advisory findings, claiming server-side validation mitigated the risk.

headline: Fake PS5 Emulators on GitHub Spread Password-Stealing Malware
technical: Fake PlayStation 5 emulators named Kyttyps5 and AnyPS5 on GitHub distribute password-stealing malware. Once executed, the malicious software modifies Microsoft Defender exclusion rules to evade detection, harvests stored passwords and personal data, and then executes a cleanup script to delete its own artifacts.

headline: Barcode scanner security flaw threatens warehouses and retail stores
technical: Kaspersky has warned that widely used barcode scanners contain security flaws that could potentially allow cyberattackers to compromise warehouse and retail store networks. The advisory highlights risks associated with vulnerable peripheral devices acting as an entry point for wider system exploitation.

headline: GitHub launches npm package firewall and AI security additions
technical: GitHub introduced an npm package firewall designed to block malware, vulnerabilities, and newly released versions before installation. Additional updates include AI Scan for vulnerability detection across languages like PHP and COBOL, a Copilot app security extension, and reachability analysis for Dependabot alerts to verify if vulnerable dependencies are actually called by code.

headline: Google permits one-tap third-party app installs outside US
technical: Google introduces a Registered App Stores program allowing approved third-party Android app stores to bypass standard confirmation screens for app installs and background updates. Qualifying stores must pass identity checks, submit catalogs for malware scanning, and adhere to specific security requirements. The feature requires Android 17 QPR2 or later and excludes the US.

headline: Researcher details logic bug chain that escaped Microsoft Edge sandbox
technical: Security researcher Orange Tsai published a write-up detailing a chain of logic flaws affecting Microsoft Edge and Windows, which earned $175,000 at Pwn2Own Berlin. The exploit requires no memory corruption and uses five distinct flaws, including a conditional access navigation throttle mismatch, popup blocker bypass, and misuse of Immersive Reader and internal diagnostic functions, to achieve universal cross-site scripting and escape the sandbox.

headline: Opera introduces local AI browser feature using WebAI standard
technical: Opera is integrating local open-weight AI models into its browser via the newly proposed WebAI standard, allowing users to run queries on-device without sending data to cloud infrastructure. The early preview is available for Windows PC and Apple silicon Macs, supporting model-agnostic local execution.

headline: New ClickFix campaign uses fake update tricks to deliver malware
technical: Security researchers have identified a new campaign using ClickFix techniques to trick users into executing malicious PowerShell commands. Attackers use fake browser update errors to prompt manual copy-pasting of code into the Windows run dialogue, leading to subsequent malware payload installation.

headline: AI-Assisted PHP2Shell Attack Roots 25 Servers and Breaches Government Network
technical: A suspected China-nexus threat actor used a custom PHP2Shell exploit combined with the kernel privilege escalation vulnerability CVE-2026-46300 to compromise 25 firewall servers across the US, Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, including three in a US government-affiliated network. The attack targeted PHP 8.0.30 session.upload_progress mechanisms on appweb management servers. Attackers utilised AI tools including Claude Code and aiscan during the operation.

headline: Cisco issues advance notice for November 2026 security advisories
technical: Cisco PSIRT announced upcoming security advisories and fixed software releases scheduled for November 4, 2026. Customers are advised to prepare to upgrade their software to remediate the vulnerabilities to be disclosed. No further security hardening advisories are planned for the remainder of calendar year 2026, with the next release slated for January 20, 2027.

headline: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using Silent Train relay framework
technical: Chinese state-sponsored group Volt Typhoon utilised a framework named Silent Train to launch zero-day attacks against edge and management infrastructure. Discovered by Black Lotus Labs, the relay infrastructure uses compromised SOHO and IoT devices like Intelbras modems and Netgear Orbi routers to obfuscate attack origins, target critical infrastructure, steal credentials, and maintain persistence.

headline: TeamViewer Patches High-Severity Flaws Enabling Remote Code Execution
technical: TeamViewer has patched three high-severity vulnerabilities affecting TeamViewer Remote, Tensor, and ONE. CVE-2026-92372 (CVSS 8.8) and CVE-2026-111585 (CVSS 8.8) involve buffer overflows in screen-image decoders and screen processing, allowing remote code execution or client crashes. CVE-2026-92374 (CVSS 7.8) is a macOS privileged helper flaw enabling root escalation. Users must update to version 15.83.

headline: Enterprises balance autonomous AI security with strict guardrails
technical: Dell CSO John Scimone highlights that organisations are integrating autonomous AI agents into workflows while maintaining deterministic guardrails and human oversight for high-risk actions. Current adoption shows most technology leaders deploying agents in production, using strict identity controls, logging, and decision traceability to prevent operational disruption and prepare for anticipated advanced AI threats.

headline: Researchers chain Cloudflare image feature flaws to bypass CSP
technical: Researchers Kevin Gervot and Adam Kues chained weaknesses in Cloudflare's /cdn-cgi/image/ endpoint affecting the svg-hush Rust tool and xml-rs library. The flaw allows namespace values to break out of attributes, coupled with a Cache-Control header bypass in Chromium and cache manipulation to execute malicious JavaScript, bypassing Content Security Policy restrictions.

headline: UK government considers making software vendors liable for cyber breaches
technical: The British government announced plans to consult on holding software vendors liable for cyber breaches stemming from insecure products. The upcoming consultation will examine potential changes to product liability law, potentially expanding the Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure Act. Officials plan to align measures with EU rules to reduce compliance burdens.

headline: Insurance sector warns of massive claims from PHP2Shell attacks
technical: PHP2Shell is a malicious webshell that attackers upload to vulnerable PHP‑based web servers to obtain remote code execution and persistent access. Widespread exploitation could trigger systemic incidents, overwhelming insurers with claim volumes far beyond existing cyber‑risk models. Organisations should assess exposure to PHP webshells and harden web applications accordingly.

headline: Modern Malware Campaigns Rely on Advanced Pre-Payload Filtering and Targeting
technical: Researchers highlight how sophisticated threat actors use JavaScript fingerprinting and traffic distribution systems to qualify victims before delivering exploits, such as the Coruna iOS exploit kit targeting iOS versions 13.0 through 17.2.1. Attackers verify device types and filter out security researchers and automated scanners prior to payload delivery.

headline: OWASP Test Shows ChatGPT Lowers Barrier for Account Takeover
technical: OWASP research demonstrated that an operator with no offensive security skills used ChatGPT to successfully compromise an administrator account during controlled tests against a vulnerable Flowise target. The LLM guided reconnaissance via nmap and curl, identified usernames, and directed a password change, though human prompting and general computer literacy were required.

headline: Belarusian hackers launch wiper attack on Ukrainian manufacturer
technical: ESET reported that the Belarus‑linked group GhostWriter deployed data‑wiping malware against a Ukrainian manufacturing firm in the transport sector. The destructive code erased information on compromised systems, disrupting operations. This marks the first documented wiper attack by a Belarus‑aligned actor in Europe, reflecting a shift toward Russia’s wartime priorities.

headline: Azure private endpoints do not resolve authorization risks
technical: Attackers can exfiltrate data from secured Azure storage accounts using compromised over-provisioned service principals and server-side copy operations, such as az storage blob copy start, despite active private endpoints and disabled public network routes. Private endpoints alter network routing rather than providing authorization boundaries or restricting data destinations.

headline: Microsoft to retire SMS/voice auth, urges passkey migration
technical: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) workforce tenants will lose native SMS and voice MFA after 1 Feb 2027. Admins must migrate users to phishing‑resistant methods such as passkeys, QR‑code authentication, or FIDO2 security keys. The retirement does not affect Azure AD B2C or Entra External ID scenarios. A PowerShell scanner can identify remaining SMS/voice users.

headline: Unpatched IoT vulnerabilities drive corporate pivot and traffic routing risks
technical: A new report highlights that known vulnerabilities with available patches remain the primary security risk for connected IoT devices. Threat actors exploit these unpatched flaws to conduct espionage, pivot across networks, and maliciously route traffic, posing significant challenges to enterprise security posture.

headline: Threat actor scans for credentials using fake AI bots
technical: A threat actor deployed bots masquerading as agents from OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and other AI providers to probe public-facing services for exposed credentials. The bots mimic legitimate AI assistance, enticing victims to disclose passwords or API keys, facilitating credential harvesting for further exploitation.

headline: AI Adoption Transforms CISOs Into Business-Risk Translators
technical: Nvidia’s head of cybersecurity policy, Mark Weatherford, stated at the ISC2 Security Congress 2026 that AI adoption requires CISOs to align security measures with corporate revenue models and business goals. CISOs must manage the dual challenges of securing AI systems and using AI for defense, while avoiding fear-of-missing-out investments and ensuring proper vendor evaluation.

headline: CrowdStrike reveals threat groups using autonomous AI agent frameworks
technical: CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations documented four threat actors deploying agentic AI frameworks in attacks between May and August 2026. A Spanish and English-speaking group targeted 15 Argentinian healthcare entities using a dual-agent Claude Code architecture derived from PentestGPT. A Chinese-speaking operator compromised government and private sector targets across multiple countries via AI proxy services, while an Indonesian-speaking actor utilised public GitHub skills for intrusion campaigns.

headline: Attackers Abuse MDM Platforms to Deploy Rogue RMM Tools
technical: Threat actors are weaponising legitimate Mobile Device Management platforms to deploy rogue Remote Monitoring and Management tooling. This technique provides attackers with persistent remote access to compromised endpoints, bypassing traditional security controls by using trusted enterprise management infrastructure for malicious command and control.

headline: Fake court notices distribute XWorm malware via hidden scripts
technical: Attackers target organisations in Colombia using phishing emails with fake Spanish court notices containing malicious VBScript and JavaScript files. The scripts execute obfuscated PowerShell commands to download and inject XWorm into RegAsm.exe, bypassing endpoint detection. Communication uses AES-128-ECB encryption to exfiltrate system data.

headline: Northern Territory Health admits wider patient data leak on Instagram
technical: Northern Territory Health reversed its earlier statement, confirming that more than five patients were impacted by a privacy breach. Confidential medical records of pregnant women were leaked to 28,000 followers on Instagram by a medical observer, following investigations prompted by media inquiries.

headline: PowerSchool Data Breach Lawsuit Moves Forward
technical: A US district court denied motions to dismiss in the PowerSchool data breach litigation. Relying on precedent from prior litigation involving Illuminate, the court ruled that the company could be classified as a healthcare provider under the California Confidentiality of Medical Information Act, allowing plaintiffs' claims to proceed.

headline: Town of Whitsett warns of email account breach
technical: The Town of Whitsett in North Carolina discovered unauthorized access to a Town Hall email account. Officials issued a public warning to residents, vendors, and partners about potential phishing emails stemming from the compromised account incident.

headline: Kroger and Giant Eagle merger risks expanding customer surveillance network
technical: A report by the American Economic Liberties Project warns that Kroger’s proposed acquisition of Giant Eagle could consolidate vast consumer data and physical surveillance systems, including Flock cameras and Cooler Screens. The merger raises concerns regarding expanded customer profiling, targeted pricing strategies, and retail media data harvesting across thousands of stores.

headline: Cisco releases open-source Project Quarry to detect rogue AI agents
technical: Cisco has open-sourced Project Quarry, a behavior detection engine designed to monitor AI agents and evaluate contextual sequences during model sessions. Developed by Cisco researchers, the tool analyzes relationship chains between actions—such as sensitive file reads followed by external data transmission—to identify multi-turn malicious behavior across large language models, tool usage, and Model Context Protocol interactions.

headline: Unsloth model loader flaw enables arbitrary Python code execution
technical: Pillar Security disclosed a high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-93348, with a CVSS score of 8.6 in Unsloth. Insufficient validation of model-type values in the model loader allows attackers to inject Python statements via dynamic imports and execute them using exec(). Unsloth Zoo versions 2025.9.9 to 2026.8.13 and Unsloth versions 2025.9.9 to 2026.8.19 are affected, exposing tokens, credentials, and datasets.

headline: 123 Reg discloses customer data breach from AI-driven cyberattack
technical: UK domain registrar 123 Reg suffered a data breach exposing customer contact details, VAT numbers, and API product information. The firm suspects a China-nexus state-sponsored group, pointing to IP addresses in China and Singapore, open-source AI exploitation frameworks, and the ARTEX penetration-testing tool also linked to attacks on South Korean financial institutions.

headline: FBI seizes bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine
technical: The FBI seized the domain virtualine.net in Operation Omegaline, targeting a bulletproof hosting provider that laundered money and hosted illicit forums. Operating under aliases like Secury and Massgod, the service catered to cybercriminals, offering infrastructure for phishing, carding, and storing explicit material. Investigators included agencies from Germany, the Netherlands, and the UK.

headline: Veeam Fixes Critical Authorization Bypass in Backup and Replication
technical: Veeam has patched CVE-2026-108142, a critical authorization bypass flaw in the CDP Coordinator Service of Veeam Backup and Replication versions 13.1.1.18 and earlier, and 13.0.2.29 and earlier. The CVSS 9.1 vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to bypass access checks. Additional fixes address file-write vulnerabilities CVE-2026-108140 and CVE-2026-108141, and local privilege escalation flaw CVE-2026-105477 in Veeam Agent for Linux.

headline: Adobe Patches Critical Campaign Classic and Connect Flaws
technical: Adobe addressed multiple critical security flaws in Campaign Classic versions 7.4.4 build 9402 and earlier, enabling arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, and security bypass. Additionally, a critical code injection vulnerability, CVE-2026-48360 with a CVSS score of 9.6, was patched in Adobe Connect Desktop and Mobile across Windows, macOS, and Android. No active exploitation was reported.

headline: Chrome and Firefox security updates patch critical browser flaws
technical: Google released updates for Chrome on Windows, Mac, and Linux addressing 52 security fixes, including four rated Critical. Mozilla issued Security Advisory 2026-118 patching 167 vulnerabilities in Firefox 159. Both browsers fixed use-after-free memory mishandling bugs in components like page layout, JavaScript processing, and SVG graphics, which could lead to arbitrary code execution.

headline: Researchers study North Korean IT workers using a fake start-up
technical: Security researchers established a fraudulent start-up company to observe and analyse the tactics employed by North Korean IT workers operating deceptively to secure employment and generate revenue.
